title: Aseptic Process Simulation (APS) Using a Filling Isolator
note: Questions derived from actual exam session 2026-04-10

questions.question: Before performing an isolator APS, can the VHP decontamination cycle be included and run as part of the APS? Explain why.
key_points: The VHP cycle must be validated in an independent study using biological indicators (BI)
APS is not used to validate the VHP decontamination cycle; each has a separate validation responsibility

questions.question: The commercial batch size is 8,000 units. According to the guidance, how many units must be filled with media at minimum for this isolator APS?
questions.explanation: An isolator APS is recommended to include at least 10,000 filled, integral units. Going below this number is not recommended, even when the commercial batch contains only 8,000 units.

questions.question: Which of the following is a Type 1 Inherent Intervention that must be simulated in an isolator APS?

options.A: Manually adjusting the filling needle because of a mechanical fault during production
options.B: Replacing an EM plate through a glove port
options.D: Switching the filling speed from low to high

questions.explanation: Type 1 interventions are unavoidable parts of routine operations and include replacing EM plates through a glove port, replenishing components, and RTP transfers. A is a Type 2 corrective intervention; C is a shift handover outside the isolator and need not be included; D is a process parameter setting.

questions.question: Which statement is correct regarding worst-case determination for an isolator APS?

options.A: The more people in the room outside the isolator, the higher the contamination risk, so this should be included as a worst case
options.B: A shift handover outside the isolator is a worst-case condition
options.C: In some situations, fewer operators may represent a higher-risk worst case
options.D: A faster filling speed is the worst case for every container type

questions.explanation: When fewer operators perform the same interventions, their movements may be larger and faster, potentially causing greater disturbance to critical areas. The true worst case must be determined through risk assessment rather than assuming that more people is automatically the worst case. A and B do not apply because of the physical barrier; the slowest speed is the worst case for the largest container, which has the longest opening exposure.

questions.question: After APS filling and before incubation, in which situation should a container be excluded from the incubation batch?

options.A: The media contains slight suspended particles
options.B: The fill volume is low (the container is not full)
options.C: The stopper is incompletely inserted (not sealed)
options.D: There is a minor visible scratch on the container wall

questions.explanation: Only non-integral containers may be excluded, including broken glass, missing stoppers, poor crimping, and empty containers. Low volume, particles, and cosmetic defects cannot be used as exclusion reasons because doing so could conceal genuine contamination.

questions.question: Three turbid units are found after incubation of an isolator APS. The investigation confirms that the root cause was a damaged operator glove, directly related to the aseptic process. What is the most appropriate next step?

options.A: Exclude the batches involving that operator and pass the remaining batches
options.B: Declare the APS a failure, perform an RCA, and usually conduct three additional APS runs
options.C: Accept the result if contamination is below 0.1%
options.D: Immediately repeat the APS and disregard the previous result

questions.explanation: The result may be accepted only when the cause of contamination is unrelated to the simulated aseptic process. A damaged glove is directly related to the aseptic process, so this APS fails and requires a complete RCA plus, typically, three additional successful runs. The acceptance criterion is always zero contaminated units; there is no percentage allowance.

questions.question: When performing an APS for a lyophilized product and simulating the lyophilizer vacuum step, what chamber pressure range should be maintained? Explain why the pressure must not be lower than this value.
key_points: It must not be lower than the equilibrium vapor pressure of the media at the loading temperature (for example, water at 25°C = 32 mbar)
Below this value, the media may undergo flash evaporation, affecting media performance
Freezing would also inhibit microbial growth and make the APS invalid

questions.question: Growth Promotion Testing passes, but contaminated units are found after APS incubation. What is the result of this APS?

options.D: Repeat growth promotion testing before making a determination

questions.explanation: A Growth Promotion pass shows that the media is effective and can support microbial growth, strengthening the validity of the contamination finding. Contamination means the APS fails. Only a Growth Promotion failure makes the entire APS invalid and excluded from the formal failure record.

questions.question: What is the main difference between initial L-3 qualification of an isolator operator and qualification of an operator on a traditional aseptic filling line?
key_points: Participation in an APS is not necessarily required for initial L-3 qualification
Aseptic technique proficiency can be demonstrated through other training activities, such as media manipulation exercises
The focus is on performing actions through glove ports within the restricted isolator space

questions.question: What is the greatest limitation of a piggyback APS?

options.A: A piggyback APS can be performed only on an isolator and is not applicable to a traditional line
options.B: A piggyback APS cannot serve as a standalone validation tool and must be combined with another simulation covering the start of filling
options.C: A piggyback APS cannot contain more than 5,000 filled units
options.D: Type 2 interventions in a piggyback APS are not counted in the total APS intervention record

questions.explanation: A piggyback APS simulates only the end of filling and cannot cover high-risk activities at the start of filling, such as line setup and initial component loading. It therefore cannot serve as a standalone validation tool and must be combined with an APS simulation covering the start of filling.
